document: NR-029 — Foreign Keys Naming Tables That Exist Nowhere
root_cause: The ORM named the class instead of the table. IdentityAuthority is niam_gov_authorities; UserSession is niam_sessions. Both classes exist, both tables exist, and PostgreSQL already enforced all three foreign keys against the real tables.

declarations.intent: reference the governance authority that issued the framework
reference the governance authority that verified the proofing

declarations.reachable_operation: adaptive MFA challenge bound to a login session
declarations.intent: bind an MFA challenge to the session that triggered it
declarations.width_note: Column is String(100) against a varchar(26) PK. The difference is pre-existing in the physical schema and PostgreSQL accepts it; the ORM mirrors the deployed column, so only the target name was changed.

action: Three ForeignKey target strings corrected. No migration, no schema change, no column change.

rejected_alternatives.delete_the_foreign_keys: would discard relationships PostgreSQL is already enforcing

verification: backend/tests/test_alembic_metadata_registry.py::test_every_foreign_key_names_a_table_that_exists — PHANTOM_FK_TARGETS is now the empty frozenset
consequence: One of NR-023's three blockers is closed. Remaining: NR-006 and NR-030.
